### AAMA/NAFS Performance Classification

**Performance Certification:** 
Design Pressure (DP), Performance Class, and Performance Grade (PG) are certified by a third party organization, in many cases the Window and Door Manufacturers Association (WDMA). The certification requires the performance of at least one product of the product line to be tested in accordance with the applicable performance standards and verified by an independent party


### Frame Material Specifications

**Material:** 
Duracast® fiberglass composite, the strongest material for windows and patio doors. It can withstand subzero cold, the most extreme heat and the rigorous performance requirements of a commercial building


**Thermal Properties:** 
Our fiberglass has virtually the same expansion and contraction as the glass, almost none. This helps reduce the risk for air-seal failure and provides long-term stability for dependable operation


**Construction Quality:** 
Secured with corner locks, metal fasteners and injected with sealant for added strength, durability and reliable water performance


### Finish and Coating Standards

**Powder-Coat Finish:** 
Long-lasting powder-coat finish meets AAMA 624, which is a highly-rated fiberglass coating


**Color Options:** 
Dual-color frames have White on the interior with Brown, Tan, Morning Sky Gray or Black on the exterior


### Warranty Coverage

**Non-glass Components:** 
Pella Impervia Duracast fiberglass components are covered for as long as the buyer owns and occupies the home, or ten (10) years from date of original purchase if the home is sold (transferable)


**Glass:** 
Glass coverage includes twenty (20) years for non-laminated glass, ten (10) years for laminated glass (such as HurricaneShield® or safety glass), and five (5) years for insulating glass with blinds or shades sealed inside (transferable)


**Labor Coverage:** 
Labor is only covered for the first two years


**Finish Warranty:** 
Factory-applied exterior paint is warrantied for ten (10) years (transferable)

## 4. RED FINDINGS / SAFETY CONCERNS

### Active CPSC Recalls - Product Not Affected

**Casement Window Recall (2024):** 
Pella's Architect Series venting wood and aluminum-clad casement windows recalled due to sash detachment hazard. Does NOT affect Impervia series


**Battery Ingestion Recall (2025):** 
Pella Reserve and Lifestyle Sliding Patio Doors and Lifestyle Windows recalled due to accessible button cell batteries. Affects specific Lifestyle Series products with motorized features, not standard Impervia DH


### Documented Quality Control Issues

**Multiple Grille Failures:** 
Brand new Impervia windows in our new home have had multiple between-the-glass grilles fall sideways requiring the sash to be replaced, among other quality concerns. It takes several months to resolve each issue


**Immediate Post-Installation Damage:** 
We purchased three very large Pella Impervia windows (45 sq ft) and they were installed in April of 2019. The next day we noticed many scratches and broken seals on two of the three windows


## 5. YELLOW FLAGS / AMBIGUITIES

### Industry Expert Critical Assessment

**Construction Quality Concerns:** 
Industry insiders cite "somewhat flimsy frame and less-than-stellar design" with air infiltration rate of 0.18 "not very impressive"


**Competitive Assessment:** 
The Impervia lacks the overall strength and durability when compared to other fiberglass options such as the Milgard Ultra window. However, for the same price there are better options for the consumer that will offer better long term value and performance


### WindowDog Expert Opinion

**Review Status:** 
We haven't gotten to the Pella Impervia yet, but it's on the list! Anecdotally I hear more positive feedback about the Marvins


**Marvin Comparison:** 
The Marvin Essential is the clear winner for me in this head-to-head match up


### Installation Quality Issues

**Professional Installation Challenges:** 
They were happy I didn't buy all Pella windows -- those had a lot of bowing in the frames and the plastic flanges just slide right off, so were difficult to install and needed a lot of shimming


**Operation Issues:** 
I found a neighbor in my area who had them and spoke with him about the Impervia and he said that it sticks on the weatherstripping when they try to open them. They asked the Pella installers to replace them but the company has dragged their feet on coming back out
